skills.title: Say what a community is: people who live in one place and help and depend on each other
Name people and helpers in a locality and the work each does
Explain how working and celebrating together helps everyone

expectations: A community is a group of people who live in the same place and share, help and depend on each other; it is bigger than one family.
Different people do different jobs (vegetable seller, sweeper, guard, teacher, doctor, postman) and everyone depends on these jobs.
Doing things together, like festivals, cleaning drives or tree planting, makes big jobs easier and brings people closer.
Every job, small or big, matters to the community.

misconceptions.belief: A community means only one's own family.
signs: Lists only family members when asked who is in their community
Says neighbours or the shopkeeper are 'not ours'
Thinks festivals happen only inside the house

diagnostic.prompt_en: Who all are part of your community?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Batao, tumhari community mein kaun-kaun aata hai?

options.text: Only the people who live in my house
Only important people like doctors and the sarpanch
My family, neighbours, shopkeepers, teachers and all the helpers around where I live

verified.solverAnswer: C) My family, neighbours, shopkeepers, teachers and all the helpers around where I live
verified.note: Exactly one correct option; distractors map to misconceptions; scientifically accurate; Hindi fidelity ok. Correct option is the longest (test-wise cue), cosmetic.

remediation.representation: Concentric-circle map: me, family, neighbours, locality helpers, whole locality
remediation.moveShape: Child places the people they met today on the rings; point out that the outer rings depend on each other too

misconceptions.belief: Only some jobs (doctor, teacher) are important; helpers like sweepers, guards and vendors do not really matter.
signs: Ranks jobs as 'big' and 'small'
Cannot say what would happen if the sweeper stopped coming
Dismisses the kabadiwala or safai karamchari as not helping

diagnostic.prompt_en: If the person who collects garbage from your colony did not come for a week, what would happen?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Agar tumhari colony se kooda uthane wale bhaiya ek hafte tak na aayein, toh kya hoga?

options.text: Nothing much; collecting garbage is not an important job
Garbage would pile up, smell and spread germs, so the job is very important
Only one family would have a problem

verified.solverAnswer: B) Garbage would pile up, smell and spread germs, so the job is very important
verified.note: Exactly one correct option; distractors map to misconceptions; scientifically accurate; Hindi fidelity ok. Correct option is the longest (test-wise cue), cosmetic.

remediation.representation: A 'what if they stopped' picture chain (garbage pile, flies, people falling sick)
remediation.moveShape: Run one what-if-they-stopped chain together, then let the child pick the next helper and run it alone

misconceptions.belief: Working together means everyone does the same job at the same time.
signs: Plans a cleaning drive where everyone only sweeps
Does not see that sharing different tasks is still teamwork

diagnostic.prompt_en: For a colony Diwali mela, which plan shows working together best?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Colony ke Diwali mele ke liye kaunsa plan sabse achha 'milkar kaam' dikhata hai?

options.text: Everyone makes rangoli and nobody does anything else
Some people make rangoli, some arrange food, some clean up afterwards
One family does everything so the others can rest

verified.solverAnswer: B) Some people make rangoli, some arrange food, some clean up afterwards
verified.note: Exactly one correct option; distractors map to misconceptions; scientifically accurate; Hindi fidelity ok. Correct option is the longest (test-wise cue), cosmetic.

remediation.representation: Job-split board: one big task broken into labelled boxes with different names
remediation.moveShape: Give a big task; child splits it into jobs and assigns people; contrast with the everyone-same-job plan

items.prompt_en: Name four people outside your family who are part of your community.
items.prompt_hi: Apne ghar ke bahar ke chaar log batao jo tumhari community ka hissa hain.
items.answer: Any four people from the locality who are not family, such as a neighbour, shopkeeper, teacher, sweeper, guard, doctor or milkman.
hints: Invite them to walk through their gali in their mind and say who they see
Point to who brings milk or vegetables and who guards the gate
Prompt: the person who teaches you at school is your ___
Assert: neighbours, shopkeepers, teachers and helpers are all part of the community

verified.solverAnswer: Neighbour, shopkeeper, teacher, sweeper/guard/doctor/postman (any four non-family)
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: What does each of these people do for the community: a postman, a sweeper, a vegetable seller?
items.prompt_hi: Batao, ye log community ke liye kya kaam karte hain: postman bhaiya, safai wale bhaiya aur sabzi wale uncle?
items.answer: Postman delivers letters and parcels; sweeper keeps the streets clean; vegetable seller brings fresh vegetables for people to buy.
acceptable: safai wale gali saaf karte hain
hints: Ask what they saw each person doing last time
Point to what is in the postman's bag
Prompt: the sweeper keeps our gali ___
Assert: postman delivers letters and parcels, sweeper cleans, vegetable seller brings food to buy

verified.solverAnswer: Postman delivers letters/parcels; sweeper cleans streets; vegetable seller sells fresh vegetables
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Your colony wants to plant 50 saplings for Van Mahotsav. Predict first: will the planting finish faster if one family plants all 50, or if 10 families plant 5 each?
items.prompt_hi: Colony mein Van Mahotsav ke liye 50 paudhe lagane hain. Pehle guess karo: kaam jaldi kab khatam hoga, jab ek hi family saare 50 lagaye, ya jab 10 families 5-5 paudhe lagayein?
items.answer: 10 families planting 5 each; the work is shared, so it finishes much faster and nobody gets too tired.
hints: Invite them to imagine one family digging 50 holes alone
Point to how many hands are working in each plan
Prompt: when work is shared among many people, it gets done ___
Assert: sharing among 10 families finishes it faster; that is how a community helps

verified.solverAnswer: 10 families planting 5 each finishes faster; shared work is quicker
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Predict what will happen in your gali if the people who sweep the street and collect garbage do not come for one whole week.
items.prompt_hi: Socho, agar ek poore hafte tak gali saaf karne wale aur kooda uthane wale bhaiya na aayein, toh hamari gali ka kya haal hoga? Pehle apna guess batao.
items.answer: Garbage piles up, it smells, flies and mosquitoes breed and people can fall ill; their work is very important for everyone.
hints: Invite them to picture the dustbin on day 1 and on day 7
Point to what flies and mosquitoes like
Prompt: without them, garbage would ___ and people could fall ___
Assert: garbage piles up and spreads germs; their job keeps the whole community healthy

verified.solverAnswer: Garbage piles up, smells, flies/germs spread, people fall sick
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Why do people in a colony celebrate festivals like Diwali, Eid, Christmas, Gurpurab or Pongal together? What does it do for the community?
items.prompt_hi: Colony mein log Diwali, Eid, Christmas, Gurpurab ya Pongal saath milkar kyon manaate hain? Isse community ko kya fayda hota hai?
items.answer: Celebrating together helps people know and trust each other, share happiness and help each other when someone needs it.
acceptable: log ek dusre ko jaante hain
hints: Ask how they feel about a neighbour they celebrated with
Point to what happens when you know your neighbours well
Prompt: people who celebrate together feel close, so they ___ each other in trouble
Assert: shared celebrations build friendship and trust, so people help each other

verified.solverAnswer: Brings people closer, shared joy, understanding and unity across families/religions
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Look at two pictures: (A) one family of five eating dinner at home; (B) families from a whole building meeting to fix their broken water tank. Which one shows a community working together, and what makes it different?
items.prompt_hi: Do picture dekho: (A) ek family ghar pe khana kha rahi hai; (B) poori building ki families milkar toota hua paani ka tank theek karwa rahi hain. Kaunsi picture community ka milkar kaam karna dikhati hai, aur kyon?
items.answer: B: many families who live in the same place join to solve a shared problem. A is one family; a family is only a small part of a community.
hints: Ask them to count how many households are in each picture
Point to the shared problem in picture B
Prompt: a community is many people living in one place who ___ each other
Assert: B is a community working together; one family alone is a small part of a community

verified.solverAnswer: B; many families cooperate on a shared problem, not just one household
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: A school is also a kind of community. How do different people work together so your school runs every day? Give two examples.
items.prompt_hi: School bhi ek tarah ki community hai. Alag-alag log milkar kaise kaam karte hain taaki school roz chale? Do example batao.
items.answer: Each person does a different job that helps the school: teachers teach, support staff clean and ring the bell, the guard keeps the gate safe, the van or bus driver brings children, the principal plans.
hints: Invite them to walk through a school day starting at the gate
Point to who is at the gate, who rings the bell, who is in the classroom
Prompt: the guard keeps us ___ and the teacher helps us ___
Assert: many people with different jobs together make the school run

verified.solverAnswer: Teachers teach, peon/cleaner keep school clean, principal manages, guard watches gate
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: During a heavy monsoon flood in a village, the roads are blocked for days. How could the people of the village help each other? Give two ideas.
items.prompt_hi: Ek gaon mein bahut baarish se baadh aa gayi aur raaste kai din band hain. Gaon ke log ek dusre ki madad kaise kar sakte hain? Do idea batao.
items.answer: Any two cooperative actions: share food and clean drinking water, give shelter in houses on higher ground, help elderly people and small children to safety, inform the panchayat or officials, clean drains together once the water goes down.
hints: Ask what a family would need most if water entered their house
Point to neighbours whose houses are on higher ground
Prompt: people could share ___ and give ___ to families whose houses flooded
Assert: sharing food, water and shelter and helping the weakest is how a community helps in trouble

verified.solverAnswer: Share food/water, rescue boats, shelter in higher ground/school, help sick and elderly
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Draw a circle map: yourself in the middle, your family in the next ring, neighbours in the next, and the helpers of your locality in the outer ring. Tell me who you put in each ring.
items.prompt_hi: Ek circle map banao: beech mein tum, uske bahar family, phir padosi, aur sabse bahar mohalle ke helpers. Batao kis ring mein kisko rakha?
items.answer: Middle: me; next ring: family; then neighbours; outer ring: locality helpers such as the shopkeeper, sweeper, postman, guard, doctor and teacher. All the rings together are the community.
acceptable: family andar, padosi beech mein, helpers bahar
hints: Invite them to say whom they meet every day
Point to who is family and who is not
Prompt: the kirana uncle and the postman go in the ___ ring
Assert: the community is all the rings together, not only the family ring

verified.solverAnswer: Me centre; family; neighbours; helpers (postman, sweeper, shopkeeper, doctor) outer
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'Only doctors and teachers are important in a community. The sweeper and the vegetable seller don't matter.' What is wrong with what Golu said?
items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Community mein sirf doctor aur teacher important hain. Safai wale bhaiya aur sabzi wale uncle se koi farak nahi padta.' Golu ki baat mein galti kya hai?
items.answer: Every job matters: without sweepers the streets get dirty and people fall ill; without vegetable sellers it is hard to get food. People in a community depend on each other.
acceptable: sab ek dusre pe depend karte hain
hints: Ask what their morning would look like without the vegetable seller
Point to the garbage story from before
Prompt: if the sweeper stopped coming, the gali would become ___
Assert: every job matters because everyone depends on each other

verified.solverAnswer: Every job matters; if sweeper/vendor stop, community suffers; no big/small
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Two plans for a colony cleaning day. Plan A: all 20 people only sweep and nobody collects the garbage. Plan B: some sweep, some fill garbage bags, some carry the bags to the big dustbin. Which plan works better, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Colony ki safai ke do plan. Plan A: saare 20 log sirf jhaadu lagaate hain, kooda koi nahi uthata. Plan B: kuch jhaadu lagaate hain, kuch kooda bori mein bharte hain, kuch bori bade dustbin tak le jaate hain. Kaunsa plan behtar hai aur kyon?
items.answer: Plan B, because splitting different jobs gets the whole task done; in Plan A the swept garbage is left lying around.
hints: Ask what happens to the swept pile in Plan A
Point to the three different jobs in Plan B
Prompt: working together often means doing ___ jobs that fit together
Assert: Plan B works because people share different jobs to finish one big task

verified.solverAnswer: Plan B; division of jobs, garbage actually removed
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Your little cousin Golu thinks 'community' just means 'my family'. Explain to him what a community really is, with one example from your street.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhara chhota cousin Golu sochta hai ki 'community' matlab bas 'meri family'. Use samjhao ki community asal mein kya hoti hai, apni gali ka ek example dekar.
items.answer: A community is all the people who live in a place and help and depend on each other (family, neighbours, shopkeepers, helpers), e.g. the colony planting trees or cleaning the park together.
hints: Invite them to start with who lives on their street
Point to one thing the whole street did together
Prompt: a community is bigger than a family because it includes ___ and ___
Assert: community = everyone living around us who helps and depends on each other

verified.solverAnswer: Community is a group living in one place helping and depending on each other, bigger than family; e.g. neighbours, kirana
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Last time we talked about communities. Without looking back: what is a community, and what is one thing people do together in it?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar humne community ki baat ki thi. Bina dekhe batao: community kya hoti hai, aur log usme saath milkar kya karte hain?
items.answer: A group of people living in the same place who share and help each other; for example celebrating festivals, cleaning drives or planting trees together.
acceptable: log jo ek jagah rehte aur madad karte hain
hints: Ask them to picture their colony
Point to the Van Mahotsav planting idea
Prompt: a community is people living in one place who ___ each other
Assert: a community is people of a place who share and help; they celebrate, clean and plant together

verified.solverAnswer: Group living in same place sharing and helping; e.g. festivals, cleaning drive, tree planting
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

skills.title: Name ways people communicate: talking, writing, phone, gestures, signs, pictures, sign language, Braille
Compare ways of communicating by speed, distance and who can use them
Explain that messages can be shared without words (gestures, faces, signs, symbols, touch)

expectations: Communication means sharing a message (an idea, a feeling or information) with someone who understands it.
We communicate with words (talking, letters, phone calls, text messages) and without words (gestures, facial expressions, signs, pictures, sign language, Braille).
Different ways suit different needs: some are fast, some reach far, some help people who cannot hear or see.
Sign language is a real language with fixed signs; Indian Sign Language is different from other countries' sign languages.
Listening and understanding are part of communication too.

misconceptions.belief: Communication needs words only.
signs: Says a traffic light 'doesn't say anything'
Does not count a wave, a nod or a smile as communicating
Thinks a person who cannot speak cannot communicate

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which of these is communication?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Inmein se kaunsa communication hai?

options.text: Only talking and writing
A traffic policeman's hand signal, a smile and a letter: all of these
Only using a phone, because it is modern

verified.solverAnswer: B) A traffic policeman's hand signal, a smile and a letter: all of these
verified.note: Exactly one correct option; distractors map to misconceptions; scientifically accurate; Hindi fidelity ok. Correct option is the longest (test-wise cue), cosmetic.

remediation.representation: Picture grid of silent messages: wave, thumbs-up, red light, zebra crossing, no-horn sign
remediation.moveShape: Silent guessing round: child reads the message from a picture or gesture, then names what carried it without words

misconceptions.belief: Sign language is just random hand-waving, and it is the same everywhere in the world.
signs: Calls sign language 'actions' anyone can guess
Thinks deaf people in India and Japan sign the same way

diagnostic.prompt_en: Sign language used by deaf people is...
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Deaf log jo sign language use karte hain, woh...

options.text: random hand movements that anyone can guess
a real language with its own signs and rules; Indian Sign Language is different from other countries' sign languages
not communication, because there are no words

verified.solverAnswer: B) a real language with its own signs and rules; Indian Sign Language is different from other countries' sign languages
verified.note: Exactly one correct option; distractors map to misconceptions; scientifically accurate; Hindi fidelity ok. Correct option is the longest (test-wise cue), cosmetic.

remediation.representation: Short animation of a few Indian Sign Language signs beside their meanings
remediation.moveShape: Show one sign, let the child guess, reveal it is a fixed sign learnt like a word; compare with how Hindi and English differ

misconceptions.belief: The newest or fastest way (a phone) is always the best way to communicate.
signs: Says letters and signs are useless now
Cannot name a situation where a gesture or sign works better than a call

diagnostic.prompt_en: At a very noisy railway station, how can a porter best tell you 'come this way'?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Bahut shor wale railway station pe coolie bhaiya tumhe 'idhar aao' sabse achhe se kaise bata sakte hain?

options.text: Call you on the phone
Wave his hand and point the way
He can't, because nobody can hear words there

verified.solverAnswer: B) Wave his hand and point the way
verified.note: Exactly one correct option; distractors map to misconceptions; scientifically accurate; Hindi fidelity ok. Correct option is the longest (test-wise cue), cosmetic.

remediation.representation: Situation cards (noisy station, far-away city, deaf friend, dark night) to match with the best way
remediation.moveShape: Give a situation, child picks a way, then ask 'would a phone work best here?' to loosen the always-best idea

items.prompt_en: Name five different ways people send a message to each other.
items.prompt_hi: Paanch alag-alag tareeke batao jinse log ek dusre tak message pahunchaate hain.
items.answer: Any five, such as talking, writing a letter, a phone call, a text message, email, gestures or hand signals, facial expressions, sign language, pictures or signboards, Braille.
hints: Invite them to think of how they told someone something today
Point to ways that don't need a voice, like a wave
Prompt: you can send a message by writing a ___ or making a phone ___
Assert: talking, letters, phone, messages, gestures, signs and sign language are all ways to communicate

verified.solverAnswer: Speech, letter, phone, gestures/sign, signs/pictures, email/messages, drums, bells
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: What message does each one give: a red traffic light, a finger on the lips, a thumbs-up?
items.prompt_hi: Batao, inka kya matlab hai: laal traffic light, hothon pe ungli, aur thumbs-up?
items.answer: Red light: stop. Finger on lips: be quiet. Thumbs-up: good, well done or okay.
hints: Ask what cars do at a red light
Point to what a teacher means with a finger on her lips
Prompt: a thumbs-up usually means ___
Assert: red light means stop, finger on lips means be quiet, thumbs-up means good; no words needed

verified.solverAnswer: Red = stop; finger on lips = keep quiet; thumbs-up = good/OK/well done
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Your nani lives in another city. Predict which will reach her faster, a letter posted today or a phone call, and roughly how long each will take.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhari nani doosre shehar mein rehti hain. Guess karo: aaj post ki gayi chitthi jaldi pahunchegi ya phone call? Dono mein kitna time lagega?
items.answer: The phone call reaches her at once; a letter takes a few days to travel by post.
hints: Ask how the letter physically travels to another city
Point to who carries the letter and how far
Prompt: a phone call reaches ___, a letter takes a few ___
Assert: the call is instant; the letter takes days because it is carried by the post

verified.solverAnswer: Phone call is instant (seconds); letter takes a few days
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Imagine you visit a village where nobody speaks your language and you are thirsty. Predict: can you ask for water without speaking? How?
items.prompt_hi: Socho tum ek aise gaon mein ho jahan koi tumhari bhasha nahi samajhta, aur tumhe pyaas lagi hai. Guess karo: kya bina bole paani maang sakte ho? Kaise?
items.answer: Yes, with gestures: pretend to drink from a cupped hand or a glass, or point at water.
hints: Invite them to show with their hands how they would say 'drink'
Point to how people understand actions
Prompt: you could make a ___ with your hand as if drinking
Assert: yes, gestures carry messages without words, like a drinking action

verified.solverAnswer: Yes, by gestures: cupped hand to mouth drinking, pointing, miming
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Why do railway stations use announcements, display boards AND picture signs all together?
items.prompt_hi: Railway station pe announcement, display board aur picture wale sign, teeno saath kyon lagaate hain?
items.answer: Different people need different ways: some cannot hear well or it is too noisy, some cannot read or don't know the language. Using many ways makes sure everyone gets the message.
hints: Ask who might miss an announcement
Point to a person who can't read the board
Prompt: using many ways makes sure ___ gets the message
Assert: different people need different ways, so stations use sound, words and pictures together

verified.solverAnswer: Different people receive messages differently (cannot see, hear, read, or language); redundancy
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Compare a letter and a phone call: give one thing a letter can do that a call can't, and one thing a call can do that a letter can't.
items.prompt_hi: Chitthi aur phone call ki tulna karo: ek cheez jo chitthi kar sakti hai par call nahi, aur ek jo call kar sakti hai par chitthi nahi.
items.answer: Letter: can be kept and read again, can carry a drawing or photo, needs no phone. Call: reaches instantly, you hear the voice and can answer back straight away.
acceptable: chitthi sambhaal ke rakh sakte hain
hints: Ask what their nani might do with a letter after reading it
Point to what you can't do in a letter: hear a voice
Prompt: a letter can be ___ again; a call lets you ___ right away
Assert: letters can be kept and reread; calls are instant and two-way

verified.solverAnswer: Letter: can be kept/re-read, written record, photos; Call: instant, hear voice, two-way talk
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: A friend in your class cannot hear. How could you tell them 'Let's play cricket after school'?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhari class mein ek dost sun nahi sakta. Use 'school ke baad cricket khelein?' kaise bataoge?
items.answer: Without sound: write it down, show it with gestures (batting action, point to the clock or outside), use the sign if you know it, or show a picture.
hints: Invite them to act out cricket with their hands
Point to paper and pencil
Prompt: you could ___ it down or show a batting ___
Assert: writing, gestures, pictures or signs all work without sound

verified.solverAnswer: Gestures, writing/note, sign language, pointing at cricket bat/ball mime, text/phone message
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Long ago, before phones, how could people in one village quickly warn the next village about danger? Think of things that can be seen or heard from far away.
items.prompt_hi: Bahut pehle, jab phone nahi the, ek gaon wale paas ke gaon ko jaldi se khatre ki khabar kaise dete honge? Socho, aisi cheezein jo door se dikhein ya sunaai dein.
items.answer: By loud sounds or signs seen from far: beating drums, blowing a conch or horn, ringing bells, smoke signals, or sending a fast runner or rider.
hints: Ask what sounds travel far across fields
Point to a drum or a temple bell
Prompt: they could beat a ___ or blow a ___
Assert: drums, conches, bells, smoke and runners carried messages before phones

verified.solverAnswer: Drums, smoke signals, fire/beacons, horn/conch, bells, flags, runners/messengers
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Look at three road signs on the screen: a triangle with a walking person, a red circle with a horn crossed out, a triangle with two children carrying school bags. Tell me in words what each sign says.
items.prompt_hi: Screen pe teen road sign dekho: triangle mein chalta hua aadmi, laal gol ghere mein kata hua horn, aur triangle mein bag liye do bachche. Har sign kya keh raha hai, shabdon mein batao.
items.answer: Walking person: people crossing ahead (pedestrian crossing). Horn crossed out: no honking. Children with bags: school ahead, drive slowly.
hints: Invite them to describe what they see in each sign
Point to the cross over the horn
Prompt: a crossed-out horn means ___
Assert: pictures can carry messages: crossing ahead, no horn, school ahead

verified.solverAnswer: Pedestrian crossing/people walking; no horn; children crossing/school ahead
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'Sign language is just people waving their hands. Anyone can understand it, and it's the same in every country.' Find the mistakes.
items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Sign language toh bas haath hilaana hai. Koi bhi samajh sakta hai, aur har desh mein same hoti hai.' Galtiyan pakdo.
items.answer: Sign language is a real language with fixed signs and rules that have to be learnt; different countries have different sign languages, such as Indian Sign Language.
hints: Ask whether Hindi and English are the same everywhere
Point to how a sign has a fixed meaning like a word
Prompt: sign language has to be ___, and India has its own ___ Sign Language
Assert: sign language is a real language that is learnt, and it differs by country

verified.solverAnswer: Sign language is a real language with grammar, must be learned, differs by country
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Two situations: telling your friend across a very noisy platform to come to you, and telling your aunt in Chennai that you passed your exam. Pick a good way for each. Why are they different?
items.prompt_hi: Do situation: shor wale platform ke us paar dost ko bulana, aur Chennai wali mausi ko batana ki tum pass ho gaye. Dono ke liye achha tareeka chuno. Dono alag kyon hain?

items.answer: Never share the PIN or OTP; real banks never ask for them. Hang up, and tell a trusted adult or contact the bank on its official number.
hints: Ask who should know a secret PIN
Point to the rule that banks never ask for a PIN
Prompt: a PIN and OTP must ___ be shared
Assert: never share a PIN or OTP; hang up and tell an adult

verified.solverAnswer: Never share PIN/OTP; hang up; tell bank/call helpline 1930, report to cybercrime
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Here is Ravi's saving chart: Week 1 ₹10, Week 2 ₹20, Week 3 ₹10, Week 4 ₹30. Tell me in words what happened, and how much he saved in all.
items.prompt_hi: Ye Ravi ka saving chart hai: Hafta 1 ₹10, Hafta 2 ₹20, Hafta 3 ₹10, Hafta 4 ₹30. Shabdon mein batao kya hua, aur kul kitna bachaya?
items.answer: He saved a different amount each week, the most in week 4; the total is ₹70.
hints: Invite them to read each bar or row aloud
Point to the tallest bar
Assert: he saved ₹70 in all, most in week 4

verified.solverAnswer: Saved different amounts each week; total 70
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'I have nine ₹1 coins and you have only two ₹5 coins, so I'm richer because I have more coins!' Check Golu.
items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Mere paas ₹1 ke nau sikke hain aur tumhare paas sirf ₹5 ke do. Mere paas zyada sikke hain, toh main ameer hoon!' Golu ko check karo.
items.answer: Golu has ₹9; two ₹5 coins make ₹10, so the two coins are more money. Count the value, not the number of coins.
hints: Ask how much each pile is worth
Point to 5 + 5
Prompt: nine ₹1 coins make ₹___; two ₹5 coins make ₹___
Assert: ₹10 beats ₹9; value matters, not how many coins

verified.solverAnswer: Golu has 9, other has 10, so other richer; value matters not number of coins
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Two children each get ₹50 a week. Asha spends ₹30 and saves ₹20. Bunty spends all ₹50. After 5 weeks, how much has each saved? Does saving mean not spending at all?
items.prompt_hi: Do bachchon ko har hafte ₹50 milte hain. Asha ₹30 kharch karke ₹20 bachaati hai. Bunty poore ₹50 kharch kar deta hai. 5 hafte baad kisne kitna bachaya? Kya saving ka matlab bilkul kharch na karna hai?
items.answer: Asha has saved ₹100 and Bunty ₹0. Asha still spent money, so saving means keeping some aside regularly, not never spending.
hints: Ask how much Asha keeps each week
Point to 20 × 5
Prompt: Asha saved ₹___ and still spent some each week
Assert: Asha saved ₹100 while still spending; saving is keeping some aside

verified.solverAnswer: Asha 100, Bunty 0; no, saving means spending wisely and keeping a part
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu what happens to money when we put it in a bank, and why it is safe even though the bank doesn't keep our exact notes.
items.prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki bank mein paise jama karne pe unka kya hota hai, aur bank humare wahi note nahi rakhta phir bhi paise safe kyon hain.
items.answer: The bank writes how much is ours in our account, uses the pooled money to give loans, pays us interest, and we can take out our amount whenever we need it.
hints: Invite them to start with what the passbook shows
Point to loans and interest
Prompt: the bank remembers ___ is ours and gives it back when we ___
Assert: the account records our amount; the bank lends pooled money, pays interest and returns our amount on demand

verified.solverAnswer: Bank records balance and lends money to others; rule that you can withdraw same amount; regulated
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Without looking back: name two places where we can save money, and one reason to save.
items.prompt_hi: Bina dekhe batao: paise bachaane ki do jagah, aur bachat ka ek kaaran.
items.answer: Places: a gullak (piggy bank), a bank savings account, a post office savings account. Reasons: the future, emergencies, buying something bigger.
hints: Ask where their coins go at home
Point to the bank and the post office
Prompt: we can save in a ___ or a ___ account
Assert: gullak or a bank/post office account; we save for the future and emergencies

verified.solverAnswer: Bank, post office, gullak/home; reason: emergencies
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

skills.title: Observe and describe features such as beaks, feet and leaf shapes
Link a beak or foot shape to what a bird eats or how it moves
Link leaf and plant features to where the plant lives
Tell living from non-living, including that plants are living

expectations: Different birds have different beaks because they eat different food: hooked for cracking nuts or tearing meat, long and pointed for catching fish, short and cone-shaped for seeds.
Feet suit how a bird lives: webbed feet for swimming, sharp curved claws for gripping, toes for perching or climbing.
Plants also suit their homes: spines and thick stems in deserts, needle-like leaves in cold snowy mountains, broad waxy leaves on ponds.
Plants are living things: they grow, need water and air, make their own food and make new plants.
Looking closely (observing) and recording helps us find these links.

signs: Says all birds eat grains or worms

Anything; beak shape doesn't matter

verified.solverAnswer: B) Fish, which it catches from the water

items.prompt_en: A parrot has a strong, curved, hooked beak. What kind of food is it good for?
items.prompt_hi: Tote ki chonch mazboot, mudi hui aur hook jaisi hoti hai. Ye kis tarah ka khaana khaane ke liye achhi hai?
items.answer: Cracking nuts and hard seeds and biting into fruits.
hints: Ask what a parrot is often seen eating
Point to a nutcracker
Prompt: a strong hooked beak can ___ hard nuts and seeds
Assert: the parrot's hooked beak cracks nuts and seeds and bites fruit

verified.solverAnswer: Hard food: nuts, seeds, fruit, cracking
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Match each beak to its food. Kingfisher: long and pointed. Sparrow: short and cone-shaped. Eagle: sharp and hooked. Foods: seeds, fish, meat.
items.prompt_hi: Chonch ko khaane se milao. Kingfisher: lambi aur nukeeli. Gauraiya: chhoti aur cone jaisi. Cheel/baaz: tez aur mudi hui. Khaana: beej, machhli, maans.
items.answer: Kingfisher: fish. Sparrow: seeds. Eagle: meat (it tears flesh with its hooked beak).
hints: Ask which bird lives near water
Point to which beak could tear
Prompt: a short cone beak is good for ___
Assert: kingfisher eats fish, sparrow eats seeds, eagle tears meat

verified.solverAnswer: Kingfisher-fish; sparrow-seeds; eagle-meat
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Here's a bird you may not know. It has very long thin legs and a long pointed beak, and it stands still in shallow water. Predict: what does it eat, and how does it get its food?
items.prompt_hi: Ek aisi chidiya dekho jo shayad tumne na dekhi ho. Uski taangein lambi-patli hain, chonch lambi aur nukeeli, aur woh kam gehre paani mein chupchaap khadi rehti hai. Guess karo: woh kya khaati hai aur kaise pakadti hai?
items.answer: Fish, frogs or small water animals; it stands in the water and quickly stabs or grabs them with its long beak (like a heron or egret).
hints: Invite them to look at where it stands
Point to the long beak, like tongs
Prompt: a bird standing in water with a long pointed beak probably catches ___
Assert: it catches fish and frogs with its long beak; long legs let it wade

verified.solverAnswer: Fish/frogs/small water animals; stands still and strikes with long beak
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: A cactus lives in a hot, dry desert. Before I show you, predict: will its leaves be big and thin like a banana leaf, or something else? Why?
items.prompt_hi: Cactus garam aur sookhe registaan mein rehta hai. Dikhane se pehle guess karo: kya uske patte kele ke patte jaise bade aur patle honge, ya kuch aur? Kyon?
items.answer: Not big thin leaves: its leaves are sharp spines and its stem is thick and fleshy, which stores water and loses very little water.
hints: Ask what is scarce in a desert
Point to how big leaves lose water in the sun
Prompt: in a desert a plant must save ___
Assert: cactus leaves are spines and its thick stem stores water

verified.solverAnswer: Something else: small, thin spines to save water
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Put your hand in a bucket of water and push the water, first with your fingers spread wide apart, then with your fingers pressed together like a paddle. Predict first: which way will push more water?
items.prompt_hi: Paani ki baalti mein haath daalo aur paani ko dhakelo: pehle ungliyan door-door phaila ke, phir ungliyan chipka ke chappu jaisa banake. Pehle guess karo: kis tarah zyada paani dhakelega?
items.answer: Fingers pressed together like a paddle push more water; this is how a duck's webbed feet help it swim.
hints: Invite them to feel the water on their palm
Point to water slipping through the gaps
Prompt: with no gaps, the hand works like a ___
Assert: a closed paddle hand pushes more water, just like webbed feet

verified.solverAnswer: Fingers pressed together pushes more water
verified.note: Water bucket activity; low risk, wipe spills, supervise. Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Why does a woodpecker have a strong, chisel-like beak, and toes with two pointing forward and two backward?
items.prompt_hi: Kathfodwa (woodpecker) ki chonch chheni jaisi mazboot kyon hoti hai, aur uske do panje aage aur do peeche kyon hote hain?
items.answer: Its beak drills holes in tree bark to find insects; its toes grip the tree trunk so it can cling and climb.
hints: Ask where a woodpecker finds its food
Point to how it holds onto a straight trunk
Prompt: the beak drills into ___ and the toes ___ the trunk
Assert: chisel beak digs out insects from bark; the toes grip the trunk

verified.solverAnswer: Chisel beak drills wood; two toes front two back grip tree trunk
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Compare a duck's feet and a hen's feet. What is different, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Batakh ke pair aur murgi ke pair mein kya farak hai, aur kyon?
items.answer: A duck has webbed feet for swimming; a hen has separate toes with claws for walking and scratching the ground for food.
hints: Ask where each bird spends its day
Point to the skin between the duck's toes
Prompt: the duck's feet are for ___, the hen's for ___ the ground
Assert: webbed feet swim; clawed toes walk and scratch for food

verified.solverAnswer: Duck: webbed for swimming; hen: separate toes with claws for scratching ground
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: A lotus grows in ponds. Its leaves are big, round and flat, with a waxy top where water drops roll off. How does this help the lotus?
items.prompt_hi: Kamal talaab mein ugta hai. Uske patte bade, gol aur chapte hote hain, aur upar se mome jaise, jahan se paani ki boondein lud jaati hain. Isse kamal ko kya fayda hai?
items.answer: The broad flat leaves rest on or above the water and catch lots of sunlight; the waxy coat keeps water from soaking or sitting on them.
hints: Ask what a leaf needs from the sky
Point to the water drops rolling off
Prompt: flat wide leaves catch ___; the waxy top keeps ___ off
Assert: broad leaves catch sunlight on the water; wax keeps them dry

verified.solverAnswer: Water rolls off so leaves stay clean/dry, don't get waterlogged and float
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Pine trees grow in cold, snowy mountains like those in Himachal. Their leaves are thin and needle-like. Why might needle leaves help in heavy snow?
items.prompt_hi: Cheed (pine) ke ped Himachal jaise thande, barfeele pahadon mein ugte hain. Unke patte patle, sui jaise hote hain. Bhaari barf mein sui jaise patte kaise madad karte honge?
items.answer: Snow slides off thin needles easily, so branches don't get loaded and break; needle leaves also lose less water in cold, dry winds.
hints: Ask what would happen to a big flat leaf covered in snow
Point to how snow piles up on flat surfaces
Prompt: on thin needles, snow ___ off
Assert: snow slides off needles so branches don't break, and they lose less water

verified.solverAnswer: Snow slides off, doesn't pile up and break branches
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Draw (or describe) a bird that lives on water and eats fish. What beak and what feet will you give it?

items.answer: A beak suited to catching fish (long and pointed, or hooked at the tip) and webbed feet for swimming.
hints: Invite them to think of a duck and a kingfisher together
Point to what helps swimming and what helps catching fish
Prompt: feet for swimming are ___; a beak for fish is ___
Assert: webbed feet to swim and a fish-catching beak

verified.solverAnswer: Long pointed beak, webbed feet
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'A neem tree is not a living thing. It can't walk and it doesn't eat.' Find the mistake.
items.prompt_hi: Golu kehta hai: 'Neem ka ped jeevit nahi hai. Woh chal nahi sakta aur khaata bhi nahi.' Galti pakdo.

Point to new leaves and seeds

Assert: trees grow, make food and reproduce, so they are living

verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Explain to your little cousin Golu why a parrot and a kingfisher have different beaks.

Point to the tool each beak is like

Assert: each beak is shaped for the bird's food

verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Quick memory check: what is special about a duck's feet, and what do they help it do?

items.answer: Webbed feet, which push water like paddles and help it swim.

Point to the skin between the toes
Prompt: a duck's feet are ___ and help it ___
Assert: webbed feet help the duck swim

verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

verified.solverAnswer: Plants make their own food using sunlight; all animals depend on them

items.prompt_en: Compare a cow's teeth and a tiger's teeth. How does each match what the animal eats?

verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.answer: Yes: the sides of the tongue can taste sweet too; all parts of the tongue can sense all tastes.
hints: Invite them to notice the taste after a few seconds
Point to taste buds being all over the tongue
Prompt: taste buds for sweet are ___ over the tongue
Assert: yes, you taste sweet on the sides too; there's no tongue map

verified.solverAnswer: Yes, taste buds across tongue (tongue map myth), sweet detected on sides
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Shake a sealed packet of chips without opening it. Predict: is the packet full of chips? What fills the rest?
items.prompt_hi: Chips ka band packet bina khole hilao. Guess karo: kya packet chips se bhara hai? Baaki jagah mein kya hai?
items.answer: No: a lot of the space is gas (nitrogen) that is put in to keep the chips fresh and stop them from breaking, so there are fewer chips than the packet size suggests.
hints: Ask how the packet feels when you squeeze it
Point to the puffed-up shape
Prompt: the packet is puffed up with ___
Assert: much of the packet is gas, added to keep chips fresh and unbroken

verified.solverAnswer: Mostly air (nitrogen), not full of chips; protects chips
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Why is it okay to eat junk food only once in a while, not every day?
items.prompt_hi: Junk food kabhi-kabhi theek hai, par roz nahi. Aisa kyon?
items.answer: It has too much salt, sugar and fat and very little body-building or protective food; eaten often it can cause weight gain, tooth decay, tiredness and illness, and leaves less room for healthy food.
acceptable: healthy khaane ki jagah nahi bachti
hints: Ask what is mostly in chips and cold drinks
Point to what is missing from them
Prompt: junk food has lots of ___ but little ___
Assert: junk food is high in salt, sugar and fat and low in nutrition, so keep it rare

verified.solverAnswer: Too much salt, sugar, fat, no nutrients; causes obesity, tooth decay, illness
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Compare a whole orange and a glass of packaged orange drink. Which keeps you full longer, and which has fibre?
items.prompt_hi: Ek poora santra aur ek glass packet wali orange drink ki tulna karo. Kaun zyada der tak pet bhara rakhta hai, aur kismein fibre hai?
items.answer: The whole orange: it has fibre, which fills you up and helps digestion; the drink has little fibre and often added sugar.
hints: Ask what the white threads and pulp in an orange are
Point to what's left when juice is made
Prompt: whole fruit has ___
Assert: the orange has fibre and keeps you full; the drink is mostly sugary water

verified.solverAnswer: Whole orange keeps full longer and has fibre; drink has little/no fibre, added sugar
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: A juice pack's ingredients say: 'Water, sugar, mango pulp (10%), ...'. What is in it the most, and is it mostly fruit?
items.prompt_hi: Ek juice pack pe ingredients likhe hain: 'Paani, cheeni, aam ka pulp (10%), ...'. Isme sabse zyada kya hai, aur kya ye zyadatar phal hai?
items.answer: Mostly water, then sugar; only 10% is mango. It is mostly sugary water, not fruit.

Point to the rule: biggest amount first
Prompt: the first ingredient is the ___ amount
Assert: water first, sugar second, only 10% mango: mostly sugar water

verified.solverAnswer: Water most; no, mostly water and sugar
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Golu says: 'This biscuit packet shows fresh milk and wheat fields, so it must be healthy.' Fix his thinking.

verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: From last time: why is a fresh fruit better than packaged juice?

items.answer: Fresh fruit has fibre and no added sugar; packaged juice often has added sugar and little fibre.

verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

skills.title: Explain why sleep matters and roughly how much a child needs

expectations: Children need plenty of sleep, about 9 to 12 hours a night, to grow, to remember what they learnt and to feel fresh.

Everyone has feelings like happy, sad, angry, scared and worried; all of them are normal and they pass.
Talking about feelings with someone we trust (parents, family, a teacher, a friend) helps us feel better.
Bright screens just before bedtime make it harder to fall asleep.

verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Sit still and put your hand on your chest to feel your heartbeat. Then do 20 jumping jacks on a clear, open floor. Predict first: will your heartbeat be faster, slower or the same after jumping?
items.prompt_hi: Chupchaap baith ke seene pe haath rakho aur dhadkan mehsoos karo. Phir khuli, saaf jagah pe 20 jumping jacks karo. Pehle guess karo: jumping ke baad dhadkan tez hogi, dheemi, ya waisi hi?
items.answer: Faster: exercise makes the heart pump faster to send more blood and air to the working muscles.

Point to the muscles needing more blood

Assert: the heart speeds up to feed working muscles; exercise trains the heart

verified.solverAnswer: Faster
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Two children have a test the next morning. One sleeps at 9:30 pm; the other watches a phone till midnight. Predict who will remember answers better and feel fresher.
items.prompt_hi: Do bachchon ka agle din test hai. Ek raat 9:30 baje so jaata hai, doosra aadhi raat tak phone dekhta hai. Guess karo, kise jawab zyada yaad rahenge aur kaun fresh mehsoos karega?
items.answer: The one who slept at 9:30: good sleep helps the brain store what was learnt and keeps you alert.

Point to what the brain does during sleep

items.prompt_en: Why does playing outside every day help both your body and your mind?
items.prompt_hi: Roz bahar khelna body aur mann dono ke liye achha kyon hai?
items.answer: Body: muscles and bones get stronger and the heart and lungs work well. Mind: you feel happier and calmer, sleep better and make friends.

Point to what running does for the heart
Prompt: play makes the body ___ and the mind ___
Assert: daily play builds the body and lifts the mood

items.prompt_en: Compare how you feel in the morning after a full night's sleep and after sleeping very late. What is different?

verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Your dadaji says he feels stiff and tired after sitting all day. Using what you know about exercise, what would you suggest, and why?

Explain why wasting food wastes everyone's work, water and land, and how to avoid waste safely

expectations: Grains like wheat go through many steps: sowing seeds, watering and growing, harvesting, threshing to separate the grain, winnowing to blow away the husk, storing, transporting, grinding into atta and cooking.
Many people work along the way: farmers, labourers, truck drivers, shopkeepers, the chakki-wala and the cook.
Each step uses water, land, time, fuel and effort, so wasting food wastes all of that.
We can avoid waste by taking only what we can eat, storing food properly and using safe leftovers in new dishes.
Spoiled food (sour smell, mould, left out too long) must not be eaten; peels and scraps can go to compost.

items.answer: Kite: the wind pushes it up and the string pulls it. Swing: a push from someone or from your own legs. Football: a kick, which is a push.
hints: Ask what happens to a kite when the wind stops
Point to who starts the swing moving
Prompt: a football moves when we ___ it
Assert: wind pushes the kite, a push moves the swing, a kick moves the ball

verified.solverAnswer: Kite: wind pushes and string pulls; swing: push/pull and gravity; football: kick push
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Make a paper helicopter: take a strip of paper, tear it halfway down the middle to make two wings, fold one wing forward and one back, and fold the bottom up a little. Stand on the floor and drop it from as high as you can reach. What does it do?
items.prompt_hi: Kaagaz ka helicopter banao: kaagaz ki ek patti lo, beech se aadhe tak phaado taaki do pankh banein, ek pankh aage aur ek peeche modo, aur neeche ka hissa thoda upar mod do. Zameen pe khade hokar jitna upar haath jaaye wahan se girao. Kya hota hai?
items.answer: It spins round and round as it falls slowly; the air pushes on its wings and turns it.

Point to the two wings

Assert: it spins as it falls because air pushes on its angled wings

items.prompt_en: Clip a paper clip to the bottom of your paper helicopter. Predict: will it fall faster or slower than before?

items.answer: Faster: the extra weight pulls it down harder compared with the air pushing up on the wings.

Point to what the clip adds
Prompt: more weight means it falls ___
Assert: the clip makes it fall faster

verified.solverAnswer: Faster
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Make one helicopter with long wings and one with short wings from the same paper. Predict which one falls more slowly.

items.answer: The long-winged one: bigger wings catch more air, so it falls more slowly.
hints: Invite them to drop both at the same time
Point to how much air each wing can catch
Prompt: bigger wings catch ___ air
Assert: long wings catch more air and fall more slowly

verified.solverAnswer: Long wings fall slower
verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Roll the same ball with the same push on a smooth floor and on a carpet or durrie. Predict where it will go farther.

items.answer: On the smooth floor: the carpet rubs against the ball more (more friction) and slows it down sooner.
hints: Ask them to mark where it stops each time
Point to the rough threads of the carpet

Assert: it rolls farther on the smooth floor because there is less rubbing

verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: You run with a phirki, first slowly and then fast. Predict: when will it spin faster?
items.prompt_hi: Tum phirki leke daudte ho, pehle dheere phir tez. Guess karo: kab zyada tez ghoomegi?
items.answer: When you run fast: more air pushes on the blades, so it spins faster.
hints: Ask what they feel on their face when running fast
Point to the air hitting the blades

Assert: running faster pushes more air on the blades, so it spins faster

items.prompt_en: Why doesn't a phirki spin when you hold it still in a closed room?
items.prompt_hi: Band kamre mein phirki ko seedha pakad ke khade raho toh woh kyon nahi ghoomti?
items.answer: There is no moving air to push its blades; it needs a push from wind to turn.
hints: Ask what was different at the windy mela
Point to the still air in the room
Prompt: with no moving air, nothing ___ the blades
Assert: no wind means no push, so no spin

verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Drop a flat sheet of paper and a crumpled ball made from an identical sheet at the same time. Which lands first, and what is different about them?

items.prompt_en: Button spinner: pass a string through two holes of a big button, twist the string, then pull the ends in and out. What makes the button spin?

verified.note: Science correct, activity safe for class 4, Hindi prompt faithful to English.

items.prompt_en: Windmills on hills in Tamil Nadu and Gujarat turn their huge blades. What pushes them, and why are they built in windy places?

items.prompt_hi: Golu ko samjhao ki phirki kaise kaam karti hai aur use aur tez kaise ghuma sakte hain.

skills.title: Say that paper is made by people from plant fibres (wood, bamboo, sugarcane waste, cotton rags)

Explain why recycling and saving paper protects trees, water and energy

expectations: Paper is made by people from plant fibres, mostly wood but also bamboo, sugarcane waste (bagasse) and cotton rags; it does not grow on trees.
Steps: the plant material is broken into tiny fibres and mixed with water to make pulp, spread thin, pressed to squeeze out the water, and dried.
Old paper can be soaked and mashed into pulp again to make recycled paper.
Recycling and using both sides of paper saves trees, water and energy and reduces garbage.
Paper can be recycled a few times but not forever, because the fibres get shorter each time.
